issues.legal_issue: An executing court may stay execution under the pending-suit rule only when the decree being executed was passed by that court.
material_facts: A money decree was passed by one court and transferred to another court for execution.
The judgment-debtors filed a suit against the decree-holder in the court handling the transferred execution and obtained an order purporting to stay execution.
The property was sold in execution, and the judgment-debtors challenged the sale on the ground that execution had proceeded while the stay was in force.
issues.conclusion: The court handling the transferred execution lacked jurisdiction to stay it under Order XXI Rule 29 because the decree had not been passed by that court. Its stay order was null and void, so the sale could not be held invalid on the ground that it occurred during a valid stay.
issues.legal_principle: Order XXI Rule 29 CPC requires that the suit be pending against the holder of a decree of the court in which the suit is pending; the phrase “such court” refers to that court. Rules 26–28 distinguish the powers of a transferee executing court from those of the court that passed the decree. Sections 37 and 42 CPC do not make the transferee court the court that passed the decree merely because it can execute the decree. The court approved Inayat Beg v. Umrao Beg, distinguished Narsidas Nathubhai Vohra v. Manharsing Agarsing Thakor, explained Maharajah of Bobbili v. Narasarajupeda Srinhulu, and held Sarada Kripa v. The Comilla Union Bank erroneous; it also referred to Jang Bahadur v. Bank of Upper India, Long v. Jagwnlal, Krishtokishore Dutt v. Rooplal Dass, Masrab Khan v. Debnath, M/s Khemachand v. Rambabu, Raghvender Rao v. Laxminarasayya, Sohan Lal v. Rajmal, and M.P.L. Chettyar firm v. Vanappa.

rule.if: execution_stay_dispute and judgment_debtor_suit_pending_in_execution_court and suit_against_decree_holder and decree_passed_by_different_court

predicates.execution_stay_dispute: A party disputes the validity of a stay order made in an execution proceeding.
predicates.judgment_debtor_suit_pending_in_executio: The judgment-debtor has a suit pending in the court handling the execution proceeding.
predicates.suit_against_decree_holder: The pending suit is brought against the holder of the decree being executed.
predicates.decree_passed_by_different_court: The decree being executed was passed by a court other than the court handling the execution proceeding.

issues.definition: When a stay dispute arises in execution and the judgment-debtor’s suit against the decree-holder is pending in the executing court, a decree passed by a different court means the stay lacks jurisdiction and cannot invalidate the sale.

issues.legal_issue: An allegation that execution property sold for a low price does not establish a basis to set aside the sale when the challenge is not brought on the ground of fraud or material irregularity in conducting the sale and substantial injury is not established.
material_facts: The judgment-debtor sought to set aside the execution sale by an application treated by the courts as one under section 47 CPC, not Order XXI Rule 90 CPC.
The judgment-debtors asserted that valuable property had been sold for a low price.
The courts did not determine whether fraud or material irregularity had occurred in publishing or conducting the sale, or whether substantial injury had resulted.
issues.conclusion: The low-price contention was not open on the materials before the court because the application was not under Order XXI Rule 90 and there was no evidence or finding of sale irregularity or fraud and resulting substantial injury.
issues.legal_principle: Section 47 CPC provides for execution-related objections. Under Order XXI Rule 90 CPC, a sale may be set aside for fraud or material irregularity in publishing or conducting it only where the applicant also proves substantial injury caused by that fraud or irregularity. The court relied on these provisions and noted that the application and decisions below did not address those matters.

rule.if: execution_sale_challenge and challenge_brought_as_execution_objection and low_sale_price_alleged and no_evidence_of_sale_fraud_or_irregularity and no_finding_of_substantial_injury

predicates.execution_sale_challenge: A judgment-debtor challenges a sale conducted in execution of a decree.
predicates.challenge_brought_as_execution_objection: The challenge is presented as an objection concerning execution rather than as a claim based on fraud or material irregularity in the sale.
predicates.low_sale_price_alleged: The judgment-debtor alleges that the property sold for a low price.
predicates.no_evidence_of_sale_fraud_or_irregularit: No evidence is led to establish fraud or material irregularity in publishing or conducting the sale.
predicates.no_finding_of_substantial_injury: There is no finding that substantial injury was caused by fraud or material irregularity in the sale.

issues.definition: When an execution-sale challenge is brought as an execution objection, a low price is alleged, and neither sale fraud or irregularity nor resulting substantial injury is established, the low price alone does not support setting aside the sale.
